**Verdict:** The identity band is defensible only as a **selected-cohort bookkeeping update**, not as a forecast of remaining work. The AU band overstates what is already in hand and should be uncoupled from 76%. Gate decisions stay as given: both identity rules fail; pair02 NI bounds pass; pair03 both NI bounds fail; both carrier secondaries fail.

**Paired evidence (fixed).** Frozen candidate vs nine-file baseline, Azure only, no fitted code. Full-cohort identity: 02 +0.70pp recall / +0.41pp precision; 03 −0.63 / −0.29; pooled −0.13 / −0.03 with FP 315=315. Unscored subsets do not reverse this (02 +1.37pp recall with −0.82pp precision and carrier error **up**; 03 −0.14pp). Carrier CIs have positive upper bounds. Pair03 A/U supply 273→264 and exact 240→237. Pooled AU 14.98% is not a transfer result: 3412→2901; drop the SCN5A20129283 H558R 408-error row and it is 3004→2901 (**3.43%**). That 408 is Table2 “Number” among controls under a 2,600-allele / 1,300-person caption, not a validated person count. Keep official gold; do not describe 408 as clinically validated persons. Pair02’s carrier cut is dominated by already-scored SCN5A27566755. Omissions are zero predictions with full positive-reference error.

**What 76% / 12.15% actually are.** Continuation01 is 261/141/123 on 384 identities, recall 67.97%, AU error 576. SCN5A25163546 is **20 TP / 0 FP / 0 FN, all counts NULL**. Folding it in yields 292/143/92, recall 76.04%, precision 67.13%, **25.2% fewer FNs**. That is not a 120-paper score. **70/576 = 12.15%** is the older SCN5A20031634 AU cut already inside the old forecast; 25163546 adds **zero** count. Citing “76.04/12.15 already observed” pairs a new identity substitution with an old AU number.

**What to change.**
- Central **76%** (range **74–78%**, **19–31%** fewer FNs) is the same ±~8-identity band on 384 around the 292/384 snapshot. Relabel as **current selected substitution, remaining identity work assumed net-neutral**, not “after remaining work.” Do not spend clinical-table continuation, DOC repair, or source-cache work as if they produced the 2pp lift.
- If remaining identity work is thought to be more than ~8 TP, the upper cap is too tight; if it is small, keep 74–78% and say remaining work is not in the central.
- **AU central 15%, 10–20%:** in-hand AU is still ~12% from 20031634. Remaining count work is joins, carrier-while-A/U-unknown, and MYBPC321302287 **≤29 units (5.03% of 576) if fully recovered**. RYR225814417 is already implemented (endpoint dispute, not upside). Do not add 30059973 or 30403697. Prefer central nearer **12%**, upside **~17%** only if MYBPC3 is fully recovered; or keep 10–20% with central explicitly remaining-work-dependent. Do not keep 15% as “already observed.”
- Transfer language stays: **no confirmed recall gain**; count gain beyond the dominant row is the **3.43%** residual; **no FP cut**. Pair02 NI pass is not a win.

**Limitations that must travel with any range.** Not a CI; not corpus-wide; not the paired 240. Novel-subset sizes 97/99 mean full cohorts were not untouched. Person-vs-allele / study-attribution on 20129283 is open. 25163546 shows source identity can move recall with **no** count gain. Stochastic regression is observed (pair03). Planning only for the original hard cohort after listed remaining work.
thought:
The user wants me to review completed results and critique a proposed forecast. They explicitly say:
The proposed forecast claims a revised central recall of 76% (range 74-78%) and combined AU error reduction of 15% (range 10-20%) for the original hard cohort after remaining work. This is not defensible. The identity rule requires observed recall gain ≥1pp, recall lower bound ≥-1pp, and precision lower bound ≥-2pp. Both tranches fail these gates: pair02 observed gain is only 0.70pp and pair03 observed gain is -0.63pp with recall lower bound -2.12pp. Carrier secondary endpoints also fail for both pairs.

The  76.04% recall and 12.15% AU reduction cited in the rationale come from adding one previously unscored SCN5A25163546 result to continuation01. This is explicitly not a fresh 120-paper score and cannot be mechanically added to the paired baseline. The single H558R row at SCN 20129283 drives most of the pooled AU gain, but the source Table2 caption indicates this is a control variant among 2,600 reference alleles and 1,300 healthy people. Person-versus-allele semantics require adjudication; the 408 count cannot be treated as clinically validated.

Remaining work items are mixed: source validation and DOC repair are parser tasks; explicit patient-ID joins and carrier preservation affect counts, not identity recall. MYBPC3 21302287 contributes at most 29 affected error units (5.03% of old 576 AU error). The 19-31% fewer identity FNs band includes the already 25.2% reduction from 25163546, so the range is not evidence of additional upside from remaining work.

The 74-78% range is therefore advisory only and should be labeled as selected-paper substitution after acquiring 25163546, not as expected yield from remaining engineering. Broad reading transfer must be described as no confirmed recall gain. The paired tranche evidence shows no identity improvement and slight pooled recall decline, so the forecast overstates expected identity performance. AU count reductions are more plausible given the 12.15% already observed plus modest joins, but the 10-20% range should be tightened to 10-18% to reflect the disputed 408 row and zero count gain from 25163546. The 76% central value is defensible only if explicitly caveated as observed substitution, not remaining-work projection.
